sowhat.text: Financing stays costly, with the 10-year at 4.88% and a December hike nearly priced, but credit is calm (HY 342 bp on Friday). Lower oil and a stock rebound help energy and tech deal sentiment; power and refining asset sales (NRG, CVR) keep coming.

pitch: Monday was the best day for stocks since April. The S&P 500 gained 2.3 percent to about 7,550 and the Nasdaq rose 2.7 percent, rebounding from last week's AI selloff. Oil fell hard, with Brent down 5.8 percent to about 93 dollars and WTI near 87, as Trump called new strikes on Iran highly unlikely. The 10-year Treasury is 4.88 percent, and Fed Governor Waller said today he leans toward a December hike, so the market now prices one at about 98 percent. October CPI is out this morning. On deals, NRG agreed to sell six gas plants to LS Power for 4 billion dollars, CVR is buying two Marathon refineries for about 4.2 billion, and Marvell's roughly 115 billion dollar stock deal for Lumentum is the big tech one.

quiz.q: Where did the S&P 500 close on Monday 9 Nov?
Why did Brent fall 5.8% on Monday 9 Nov?
quiz.a: Trump said fresh US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution that could ease Gulf supply risk.

quiz.q: Who advised NRG on its sale of six gas plants to LS Power, and for how much?
quiz.a: Barclays was NRG's lead financial adviser; the price is $4B in cash.

chat.a: Monday was the best day for stocks since April: the S&P 500 rose 2.3% to 7,550 and the Nasdaq 2.7% after last week's AI selloff. Oil fell about 5% on Iran hopes, and the Fed is now seen hiking in December at about 98%.
chat.tip: Lead with the rebound, then oil, then the Fed.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $92.57 and WTI at $86.85, down 5.8% and 4.4% on Monday after Trump called new strikes on Iran highly unlikely. Brent fell 16.4% the week before, so the risk premium has come out fast. Lower and more volatile prices make energy buyers and sellers harder to match on price.
chat.tip: Name the Iran diplomacy hope as the driver.

chat.a: NRG's $4B sale of six gas plants to LS Power, about 8.0x 2027 EBITDA, with Barclays advising NRG. CVR is buying two Marathon refineries for about $4.2B, also with Barclays. Marvell is buying Lumentum for about $115B in stock, with Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman for Marvell and Citi and Evercore for Lumentum.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: October CPI on Tuesday, expected at +0.3% headline, since a December hike is already about 98% priced. Treasuries are closed Wednesday for Veterans Day, Williams speaks Thursday and PPI comes Friday. I'm also watching Nvidia earnings next Tuesday.
chat.tip: Tie CPI to the hike odds.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.88% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Companies with most of their value in the terminal value, like growth tech, fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How does a falling acquirer share price affect a stock deal like Marvell and Lumentum?
chat.a: Marvell is paying 4.5 of its shares per Lumentum share, a premium of about 24% to 28 Oct prices. The ratio is fixed, so a lower Marvell price cuts the dollar value Lumentum holders receive, while the premium was set against old prices. Boards may face pressure to revisit terms if the gap widens.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed range is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and a December hike is priced at about 98%. The 10-year is 4.88%, so debt is costly. High yield spreads were 342 bp on 6 Nov, so credit is still tight and financing is available at a price.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
